newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to invest $10 bln to cut oil imports - papers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to invest $10 bln to cut oil imports - papers.

text.p: Brazil's Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said state-owned oil firm Petrobras will invest $10 billion over the next five years to reduce oil imports, Brazilian newspapers reported on Tuesday.
Kandir said the company will invest that amount to raise oil production by at least 600,000 barrels per day, according to the Jornal do Brasil and O Globo newspapers.
Currently, Brazil imports 550,000 barrels per day (bpd) and produces over 900,000 bpd, Jornal do Brasil newspaper said.
According to Jornal do Brasil, a reduction in oil imports would help reducing Brazil's trade deficit.
The newspapers quoting Kandir did not specify if he was only referring to crude or also refined oil products when speaking about oil imports and production.

Regarding the country's public accounts, Kandir said he expects the government's operational deficit, which includes interest payments, to be below three percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) this year.
The operational deficit was 3.89 percent of GDP last year.
